- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp upward sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps >0.80 within 3 days, add 0.5–1.0 price point to forecast horizon.
- Model over-anticipates downward moves after negative sentiment; if sentiment drops below 0.20 and persists, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price > 1.5σ above historical mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point; if below 1.5σ, increase by 0.5–1.0.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 2–4 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to sentiment-weighted price adjustments.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >3% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point per day until convergence.
